=== ANTHROPIC === (5 findings)
release-notes/api literal list since 10-08:
  10-09: dynamic workflows for Managed Agents (beta, managed-agents-2026-04-01). Set agent's
         multiagent field to {"type":"multiagent_20261001","workflows":{"type":"enabled"}}.
         Follow via workflow_run.* events. Links to new page /managed-agents/workflow-runs.
  10-08: Compliance API returns unified-Claude-experience chats (REPORTED 10-08);
         Compliance API can download Claude Docs documents as WORD files (held below bar).
news Oct list: 10-08 2026 Usage Policy update / American scientific discovery / Anthropic
  Cyber Mission; 10-06 Cyber Verification Program; 10-02 $100M engineers; 10-01 Barclays.
  (All policy/PR — none reportable.)
REPORTED:
  * DYNAMIC WORKFLOWS + WORKFLOW RUNS. Agent AUTHORS A PROGRAM; Anthropic's server runs it in
    the BACKGROUND. New entity: workflow run. States running/idle/ended. result types:
    completed, stopped, program_error, thread_limit_error, timeout_error, unknown_error.
    Events: workflow_run.created (carries name + phases), .status_running, .phase_started,
    .status_ended. NO API STARTS A RUN (model judgment from user.message text) and NO API
    STOPS ONE — documented stop procedure is "send a user.message asking the agent to stop
    its runs"; archiving the session also ends runs. Anthropic states permission policies
    "apply to the tools that a run's agents call, NOT to starting the run."
    RUN THREADS ARE EXEMPT FROM THE SESSION CHILD-THREAD LIMIT.
    Budget pause: a paused run does NOT keep the session running -> session goes idle with
    budget_reached while the run is still open; the run's LIFETIME KEEPS PASSING while paused,
    so it can die with timeout_error mid-pause.
  * INLINE AGENTS ON BY DEFAULT. multiagent_20261001: subagents AND workflows both enabled by
    default; subagents.predefined_agents and workflows.predefined_agents BOTH EMPTY by default;
    inline_agents enabled under both. Agent/workflow defines agents at runtime AND WRITES THEIR
    SYSTEM PROMPTS. "You can't limit an inline agent" to declared MCP servers. Only scoping:
    inline_agents {"type":"disabled"} under BOTH + >=1 predefined agent in each (empty list =>
    400). Sending null to `workflows` TURNS IT ON (default is enabled) — watch for that.
    Two lists are separate; up to 20 agents each. An agent that itself has `multiagent` set
    cannot be listed as another agent's subagent. {"type":"self"} allowed.
  * SELF-HOSTED SANDBOX ENVIRONMENTS. config {"type":"self_hosted"} on POST /v1/environments.
    Environment = WORK QUEUE. Customer runs an ENVIRONMENT WORKER (ant CLI `ant beta:worker poll`,
    + Python/TS/Go SDK workers). NEW CREDENTIAL TYPE: environment key ANTHROPIC_ENVIRONMENT_KEY
    (sk-ant-oat01-...), CONSOLE-ONLY issuance even for API-created envs. Plus a PER-WORK-ITEM
    `secret` which is the ONLY credential the memory-store endpoints accept (env key rejected).
    Claude Platform on AWS: worker uses SigV4 + managed policy AnthropicSelfHostedEnvironmentAccess;
    Console environment keys DO NOT WORK against that endpoint.
    Session resources: memory_store ONLY. file / github_repository => 400.
    Vendor worker builds: AWS Lambda MicroVMs, Blaxel, Cloudflare, Daytona, E2B, Fly.io,
    GKE Agent Sandbox, Modal, Namespace, Superserve, Vercel.
    Independent of MCP tunnels. Tool inputs AND OUTPUTS still flow to Anthropic's control plane.
  * read_only MEMORY STORES ARE WRITABLE LOCALLY. "protected from upload, not from local
    modification." worker write/edit refuse; endpoints reject writes with the session secret;
    BUT bash, custom tools and sandbox-served MCP servers run with the worker's permissions and
    CAN rewrite /mnt/memory/. Later tool calls that session read the changed copy. Documented
    mitigation = disable bash + no filesystem-writing custom tool. Self-poisoning with no trace
    in the authoritative store. Pairs with the AgentCore IngestData silent-write gap.
    ALSO: a worker that exits without teardown LEAVES THE MEMORY COPY BEHIND on disk.
  * `auto` PERMISSION POLICY. Third type beside always_allow / always_ask. Server evaluates EACH
    call against tool + input + session content so far => allow / ask / deny. Denied: agent gets
    `Permission to use {tool_name} has been denied.` with is_error:true, session keeps running,
    CLIENT CANNOT OVERRIDE (user.tool_confirmation on a denied call => 400).
    Event field evaluated_permission + nested evaluation.evaluated_permission with reason_code
    (high_risk, indeterminate). Anthropic: reason_code is "a value for your client to branch on
    and keep in audit records."
    *** DEFAULTS: agent toolset = always_allow. MCP toolsets = always_ask. ***
    Per-tool overrides exist (`name` + policy). Custom tools are NOT governed at all.
    Running sessions keep the toolset config they were created with; updates apply to new sessions.
NOT REPORTED: advisor formalized as multiagent.advisor {"type":"enabled","model":...}, disabled
  by default — the advisor TOOL was already reported 2026-09-17, this is just its config surface.
  Compliance API Word export of Claude Docs. Usage Policy / Cyber Mission posts.
